messages:
Maria: Hey — quick Q about a Terraform change I'm planning for namespace `ml-inference-prod`. I opened a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/342. Goal: let the namespace service account read KMS-wrapped secrets in Secrets Manager.

Maria: Current plan is to create a role-per-namespace and attach a read-only KMS/SecretsManager policy. Terraform snippet in the PR: 
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "k8s_sa_role" {
  name = "redwood-ml-inference-prod-sa"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.sa_assume.json
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "sa_kms_read" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.k8s_sa_role.name
  policy_arn = var.kms_read_policy_arn
}
```

Maria: And in K8s we'll annotate the service account like `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-ml-inference-prod-sa`. Is that the right pattern or should we be doing something else?

Ajay: Quick Q: are you creating a role per namespace or trying to reuse an existing role?

Maria: Role-per-namespace. We want isolation for the prod inference workloads.

Ben: FYI if it's role-per-namespace, please follow the role name pattern we use (team-namespace-env-sa) and add the tag map. Also make sure the assume_role_policy includes the correct `sub` claim format — EKS uses `system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa>` in the condition.

Kai: small infra automation FYI — if you create new roles we need to add them to the IAM inventory and run the drift-checker. @deploy-bot can you confirm CI plan?

deploy-bot: terraform plan completed on CI: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/plan/7843 — Summary: +1 aws_iam_role, +1 aws_iam_role_policy_attachment, +1 aws_secretsmanager_secret_version. No drifts detected.

Nora: Also, for the k8s SA annotation use the exact key `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` (no extra spaces) and set the SA name in TF output so we can reference it in app manifests.

Maria: Good call. One more thing — our kubelets have projected service account token TTL = 1h. Will that break apps that mount credentials via the token?

Ben: It won't break assuming your app uses the AWS SDK with proper credential refreshing. The projected token is short-lived, but the IRSA flow uses the web identity token to assume the role and get STS creds; SDKs will refresh. If your app caches role creds longer than token TTL you'll see failures when the token rotates.

Ajay: Also check for the `aud` claim — our OIDC provider expects `sts.amazonaws.com` as audience in tokens. The assume_role_policy should allow that.

Maria: For secrets wiring, I'm planning to use ExternalSecrets (AWS Secrets Manager backend) + the Secrets Store CSI driver for mount-based reads. Terraform will create the secret version in Secrets Manager. Any objections?

Kai: That's fine. One small caution: CSI driver pods need their own SA with the right permissions, or use the controller's role. Make sure the ExternalSecrets controller has access to list/get secrets.

Nora: Left a comment on the PR about adding lifecycle ignore_changes for `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` content to avoid churn from our local tests.

Maria: Thanks — I'll address the comments, update the role name/tagging and adjust the assume policy for `sub`/`aud`, then re-run plan and ping infra-owners for review.

Ben: LGTM after those changes.

Ajay: Thanks — ping me when it's ready and I'll do a quick pass on state locking and backend keys.

Maria: Will do. :thumbsup:
